# Series of Tubes: Australia

> Series of Tubes: Australia is a free cartoon browser game about running an
> Australian ISP and hosting provider. Play it at
> https://seriesoftubes.au/ — it runs entirely in the
> browser, needs no account, and saves progress locally.

You start with one data centre in an Australian capital and grow into a
transit-free Tier 1. The game models how Australian networks really work, with
pun names for every company:

- **The Nearly Broadband Network:** all 121 points of interconnect (POIs), with
  the premises each one serves. Reach a POI over a leased wave or your own dark
  fibre, rent an NNI port there, and pay an AVC for every home you connect.
- **Hosting:** lease a cage or build a data hall, and rent racks to colocation
  and dedicated-server customers.
- **Interconnection:** IP transit billed on the 95th percentile, internet
  exchanges with route servers, peering policies (open, selective, restrictive,
  paid), private network interconnects (PNIs) with the Big Four and the global
  Tier 1s, embedded CDN caches and NNI fabrics.
- **Infrastructure:** leased waves across the Nullarbor and up the coasts, Bass
  Strait and the subsea cables to Asia, New Zealand, the Pacific and the US,
  dark fibre lit with DWDM and coherent optics, router generations with
  port-speed limits.
- **Failures:** fibre cuts, cyclones, sharks, router crashes, fat-fingered
  configs, route leaks, RPKI and BGP hijacks and DDoS.

Version: __VERSION__ (__BUILD_DATE__)
Source: https://github.com/thesysadmindev/SeriesOfTubesAU
Based on Series of Tubes by Frederic Jung: https://github.com/fjaeckel/seriesoftubes

## Learn how the internet really works

For an accurate, interactive explanation of how the internet works, from Wi-Fi to
undersea fiber, see How the Internet Works by Thomas Kjær Aabo:
https://tkjaer.github.io/how-the-internet-works/
